Subject: Post-call recap + recommended next steps (model fit & quant)

Hi Kathy —

Thanks for the call earlier. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we keep momentum: 

Call summary
- Goal: integrate LLM-assisted insights into Nova's risk-analysis pipeline with latency target ~120ms p95 and throughput ~60 req/s per GPU.
- Data: evaluation set will be your 3k “edge cases” JSONL (we discussed redaction rules).
- Primary concerns: hallucination on financial QA, and tail-regression risk when using heavier quantization.

Preliminary model-fit recommendations (based on our short-stage eval):
- Preferred: Llama-2-13B-instruct (tuned) at FP16 for highest quality baseline.
- Throughput-first candidate: Mistral-7B-512 with AWQ/GPTQ profiles (aggressive quant) — much faster but some drop on nuanced completions.
- Balanced: Falcon-40B-deploy quantized to FP8 for throughput without large quality delta on your prompts.

Attachments we shared after the call: quant-tradeoffs-matrix.xlsx (summary table), prompt-set-v1.jsonl (the sanitized prompt set we used), and a small sample awq-vs-gptq-sample-output.txt. Also linking the benchmark run: https://bench.redwood.ai/runs/NA-4872

Proposed next steps
1) We’ll provision a short dedicated eval run against your redacted 3k set (estimate 48–72h). Please confirm you can share the redacted file via the Drive link or HubSpot attachment.
2) Technical deep-dive with Aditya (ML eng) to walk AWQ/GPTQ/FP8 tradeoffs and the mitigation strategy for potential quality regressions — can we target Mon 9/6 10am PT?
3) Procurement: introduce Nova procurement contact (cc if possible) and confirm timing for any PO/terms.

Open questions for you
- Is 120ms p95 a hard SLO or a preferred target? That will affect our routing on Dedicated vs burst capacity.
- Any blacklisted tokens/phrases or extra redaction rules beyond the standard PII list?

Thanks — looking forward to next steps.

—

From: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Post-call recap + recommended next steps (model fit & quant)

Kathy —

Short technical note on AWQ vs GPTQ vs FP8 for your context (summary first, details below):

TL;DR
- Start with FP16 baseline (Llama-2-13B-instruct) to measure a quality floor.
- Run parallel FP8 quantized runs for Falcon-40B (balanced) — expect ~1–3% drop in exact-match QA metrics, but much better throughput than FP16.
- AWQ on smaller models (Mistral-7B) gives the best latency and cost per token; expect larger quality variance on long-form or multi-step reasoning (outlier failures).
- GPTQ tends to be more stable across instruction-following models than AWQ, but slightly worse throughput compared to AWQ.

Tradeoff table (high level)
- AWQ: max throughput, higher variance in edge cases. Good for stateless, high-volume calls where tail hallucination risk is low.
- GPTQ: middle ground — better stability on instruction tasks but less compact kernels than AWQ.
- FP8 (hardware-accelerated): good compromise for large models; keeps quality close to FP16 with substantial speedups on our latest runtime and FP8 kernels.

Mitigations we recommend for Nova:
1) Prefix caching for recurring prompts to reduce required tokens and tail variance.
2) Canary eval set (we’ll use 500 of your most-sensitive cases) after each quant profile run to detect regressions automatically.
3) Automated fallback policies: if the model returns low-confidence signals (entropy or logit-gap heuristics), route to FP16 fallback for that request.

Numbers from our internal bench (your types of prompts, approximate):
- Llama-2-13B FP16: p95 latency 190ms, throughput 22 req/s on A100 80GB (single stream numbers)
- Falcon-40B FP8: p95 latency 145ms, throughput 34 req/s on same hardware
- Mistral-7B AWQ: p95 latency 95ms, throughput 62 req/s

Caveats: these are illustrative; exact numbers will depend on sequence length, batching, and your prepended context size. We’ll run the 3k eval to produce a direct comparison and surface any safety/accuracy regressions.

I’ve attached a short tradeoffs spreadsheet and a sample of AWQ vs GPTQ outputs we observed on a few of your prompts. Happy to walk through in the deep-dive.

—
Aditya Rao
Applied ML Engineer, Redwood Inference
aditya_rao@redwood.com
